result.scope: R2: the architectural language and the @buildapp/architecture package (registries, proposals, authority, hypothesis pipeline, graphs, index), plus the model-schema / validator / compiler code they point at and docs/FEATURE_IDENTITY_GRAPH.md where it sets the provenance vocabulary for image-derived facts. Read-only. I opened no image or binary files and fetched nothing from the network.
missing: NOT_READ: packages/commands/src/apply-architecture.ts. I did not check how the DSL layer re-validates createAssembly/createColumn etc. beyond what the validator code shows.
NOT_READ in full: hypotheses/demos.ts bodies, fixtures/roofs.ts, fixtures/run.ts, graphs/roof-graph.ts and graphs/svg.ts internals.

NOT_READ: packages/source-vision (it exports providers/anthropic.js per packages/source-vision/src/index.ts:8, which is a remote VLM provider). It is outside R2 but relevant to the 'no remote AI' constraint and should be covered by another scope.

There are no WINDOW, EXTERIOR_DOOR, GARAGE_DOOR, RAILING/BALUSTRADE, COVERED_TERRACE, PORCH or GARAGE capability keys in the registry, so for those rows the recognition status is MISSING (not recorded), not NONE.

Nothing in the repo uses the term 'site plan' or 'interior render' in this scope. Asset/view classification vocabulary lives only in reconstruction v2 ViewFamilySchema (PLAN, ELEVATION, SECTION, PERSPECTIVE, SITE, PAGE) and has no INTERIOR/EXTERIOR or PHOTO/RENDER distinction.

claims.statement: The capability registry has 21 keys. Its recognition enum is exactly ANALYZER_V2 | SYNTHETIC_PIPELINE | NONE. Nothing in it records recognition from real images, renders or photos.
claims.evidence: `export type RecognitionStatus = 'ANALYZER_V2' | 'SYNTHETIC_PIPELINE' | 'NONE'`. The header says: 'The framework existing is not a claim that houses are recognised.'
claims.relevance: A 005R observation schema must not write into this enum. If 005R needs a research status (for example a RESEARCH_IMAGE_OBSERVATION status), that is a separate field and needs an explicit OWNER decision.

claims.statement: The published artifact agrees with the source registry. Terrace and balcony are SUPPORTED/ANALYZER_V2. Canopy, pergola, column, beam, exterior steps, entrance and unknown assembly are SUPPORTED/SYNTHETIC_PIPELINE. Carport is SUPPORTED/NONE, loggia PARTIAL/NONE, handrail PARTIAL/NONE, parapet SUPPORTED/NONE.
claims.evidence: Parsed JSON with top-level keys assemblies, capabilities, primitives, relationships, schema, schemaVersion, and printed key/status/recognition for all 21 entries.
claims.relevance: Baseline row values for the R2 table.

claims.statement: Several requested assemblies have no capability key: WINDOW, EXTERIOR_DOOR, GARAGE_DOOR, RAILING/BALUSTRADE (only HANDRAIL exists), COVERED_TERRACE, PORCH and GARAGE. For these the registry records nothing, which is different from recording NONE.
claims.evidence: The CAPABILITY_KEYS list contains no such entries.
claims.relevance: A research JSON may not cite a capability status for these. It should say 'no capability entry'.

claims.statement: The hypothesis pipeline forms hypotheses for only six families: DORMER, PERGOLA, CANOPY, CARPORT, EXTERIOR_STEPS and ROOF. Terrace, balcony, loggia, railing, window, door, garage door and porch can only end up as UNKNOWN through the pipeline. Of these, window and door appear only as OPENING evidence for DORMER and ENTRANCE.
claims.evidence: `FAMILIES = ['DORMER', 'PERGOLA', 'CANOPY', 'CARPORT', 'EXTERIOR_STEPS', 'ROOF']`. EMITTERS has exactly these six keys.
claims.relevance: Any 005R exterior class outside these six has no fusion path. The research JSON has to stay an observation layer.

claims.statement: No production package or app imports @buildapp/architecture. A test enforces this, and no package.json other than its own names it. So runPipeline/applyPipeline is never reached on a production path, and no code path today lets any detector's proposal, image-derived or otherwise, create or modify a model assembly in production.
claims.evidence: The test iterates the src of analysis-service, commands, geometry, mobile-scene, model, reconstruction, source-analyzer, source-cv, source-metrics, source-observations, source-package and editor, plus apps/local-analyzer, apps/analyzer-api and apps/web, and asserts `!spec.startsWith('@buildapp/architecture')`. Grepping package.json files found only packages/architecture/package.json:2. The only other importer is packages/editor/test/categories.test.ts:6 (test material).
claims.relevance: Answers Q3 for the architecture package: there is no image-to-assembly path.

claims.statement: Proposals are 'evidence, never objects'. The pipeline reads its context model and writes nothing. Its only product is a Building DSL program, which applyCommands re-validates.
claims.evidence: 'no detector writes the model'. PipelineInput.context is commented 'It is read, never written.' A test checks that every emitted command parses as BuildingCommandSchema.
claims.relevance: Design pattern for 005R: an observation JSON that links to proposals keeps the same no-write contract.

claims.statement: SemanticProposal is the type a research observation should link to. It has these fields: { id, kind: ProposalKind, geometry: ProposalGeometry, confidence 0..1, sourceFrameId, detector: Detector, authority: SourceAuthority, featureKey?, note? }. The schema is strict (unknown fields are refused), and parseProposals refuses invalid or duplicate entries rather than repairing them.
claims.evidence: `.strict()`; `return dup ? { ok: false, errors: [...] }`
claims.relevance: Because the schema is strict, a 005R record cannot add fields such as assetId or projectVersion to a SemanticProposal. It needs its own envelope that references proposal ids, sourceFrameId and featureKey.

claims.statement: ProposalGeometry holds only world-space metric geometry: POLYGON (Vec3 points), SEGMENT (Vec3 start/end with optional width/depth) or VALUE (quantity/value/tolerance). There is no pixel or image-space geometry and no asset, page, revision or pixelRect field.
claims.evidence: `const Vec3 = z.object({ x: z.number().finite(), y: ..., z: ... })`; the discriminated union is POLYGON | SEGMENT | VALUE.
claims.relevance: An image classifier or detector output with only pixel boxes cannot be a SemanticProposal without a metric registration step. The 005R JSON should hold pixel-space observations natively and link to proposals only where registration exists.

claims.statement: PROPOSAL_KINDS has 13 drawing-level evidence kinds: ROOF_PLANE_REGION, ROOF_LINE, ROOF_INTERRUPTION, VERTICAL_FACADE, OPENING, VERTICAL_MEMBER, HORIZONTAL_MEMBER, COVER_SURFACE, NO_COVER_OBSERVED, STEP_EDGE, LEVEL_SURFACE, PRINTED_DIMENSION, UNCLASSIFIED_GEOMETRY. None of them is a railing/guard, a garage door, a window-vs-door distinction, a balcony or a terrace.
claims.evidence: Enum literal list.
claims.relevance: The 14 requested 005R assembly classes do not map 1:1 onto proposal kinds. The JSON should carry its own assembly label and an optional list of proposal-kind links.

claims.statement: DETECTORS = DETERMINISTIC_CV, OCR, ML_FLOORPLAN, VLM, OWNER, SYNTHETIC. There is no value for a local non-VLM image classifier (for example a classical feature or small CNN router).
claims.evidence: Enum literal.
claims.relevance: A local router would have to be reported as DETERMINISTIC_CV or ML_FLOORPLAN, and neither describes it accurately. Flag this rather than extend the enum (production change, out of scope).

claims.statement: SOURCE_AUTHORITIES ranks PRINTED_DIMENSION > TECHNICAL_GEOMETRY > CROSS_VIEW > PERSPECTIVE > VISUAL_INFERENCE > CONVENTION. PERSPECTIVE and VISUAL_INFERENCE both resolve to model status VISUAL_INFERRED. Only SOURCE_EXACT and SOURCE_CORROBORATED count as hard metric evidence.
claims.evidence: `case 'PERSPECTIVE': case 'VISUAL_INFERENCE': return 'VISUAL_INFERRED'`; `HARD_EVIDENCE_STATUSES = ['SOURCE_EXACT', 'SOURCE_CORROBORATED']`
claims.relevance: A render-derived fact can carry at most authority PERSPECTIVE, which becomes model status VISUAL_INFERRED and never counts as hard evidence.

claims.statement: The BuildApp language does NOT forbid metric values from perspective renders. PERSPECTIVE is a legal QuantityCandidate authority with a default tolerance of 0.25 m. It wins when no higher authority states the quantity. It never overrides a higher one: a disagreement is recorded as a conflict and never averaged in.
claims.evidence: DEFAULT_TOLERANCE has `PERSPECTIVE: 0.25`. The conflict reason reads '... does not override ...'. The doc says: 'A render never overrides a printed dimension, however many renders agree.'
claims.relevance: This conflicts with the stricter rule in /home/user/BuildPlan-PC-Legacy/CLAUDE.md:451-453 ('Obraz perspektywiczny nie ustala żadnego wymiaru'). 005R should adopt the stricter rule for its JSON (no metric fields from EXTERIOR_RENDER/PHOTO) and report the divergence.

claims.statement: The pipeline demos and tests do use render metrics. The pergola demo feeds a PERSPECTIVE post height that loses to a higher authority, and the test asserts that a conflict with lost.authority PERSPECTIVE is recorded. The roof demo feeds a render 'PRINTED_DIMENSION' pitch (detector VLM, authority PERSPECTIVE).
claims.evidence: `const render = (p) => ({ confidence: 0.6, detector: 'VLM', authority: 'PERSPECTIVE', ...p })`; `render({ id: 'pitch-render', kind: 'PRINTED_DIMENSION', ... value: pitchDeg + 3 })`
claims.relevance: Shows the intended treatment: render values are lowest-but-one evidence and are kept as conflicts. Note that PRINTED_DIMENSION kind combined with PERSPECTIVE authority is allowed by the schema, so the 'printed' label does not imply print-level authority.

claims.statement: Fusion rules: the most specific viable family is ACCEPTED unless a rival of equal specificity scores within 0.1, or the group is 'visualOnly'. visualOnly means fewer than 2 frames and every authority ranked at or below VISUAL_INFERENCE. UNKNOWN requires at least 2 spatial proposals and (at least 2 frames or one technical-authority proposal). Anything else is REJECTED and emits nothing.
claims.evidence: `const visualOnly = group.frames.length < 2 && ps.every((p) => authorityRank(p.authority) >= authorityRank('VISUAL_INFERENCE'))`; `const realFeature = spatial.length >= 2 && (group.frames.length >= 2 || technical)`
claims.relevance: This is an abstention model 005R can mirror: one visual reading in one frame is a hint, not an object.

claims.statement: PERSPECTIVE (rank 3) is not counted as 'visualOnly' (which needs rank >= 4, VISUAL_INFERENCE). So a single-render group of PERSPECTIVE proposals can be ACCEPTED for families without a crossView requirement: PERGOLA (2 VERTICAL_MEMBER + 3 HORIZONTAL_MEMBER + 1 NO_COVER_OBSERVED), CARPORT, EXTERIOR_STEPS and CANOPY (subject to emitter preconditions). Only DORMER and COLUMN demand crossView.
claims.evidence: Code reading only. The existing test (hypotheses.test.ts:39-45) covers the DORMER case, which fails only because of crossView.
claims.relevance: To test: remap demoPergola.proposals() to sourceFrameId 'render-1', authority PERSPECTIVE, detector VLM, run runPipeline, and check whether decision === 'ACCEPTED'. If it is, a single render can state a pergola assembly, which matters if 005R observations are ever fed into proposals.

claims.statement: The assemblies emitted for pergola, canopy, carport and entrance, and their relationships, are hard-coded to authority CROSS_VIEW, giving model status GEOMETRIC_INFERRED. This does not depend on the authorities of the proposals behind them. Members and cover use the resolved authority, so a perspective-only member becomes VISUAL_INFERRED. Unknown assemblies are forced to VISUAL_INFERRED and FRAGMENTARY.
claims.evidence: `evidence(ctx, h, ps, 'CROSS_VIEW', false, 'pergola')`; `case 'CROSS_VIEW': return 'GEOMETRIC_INFERRED'`
claims.relevance: Combined with C15, a render-only pergola assembly could be labelled GEOMETRIC_INFERRED. This is a provenance overstatement risk worth a test, but not a production change in 005R.

claims.statement: Exclusions ignore authority. Any proposal whose kind is in cap.exclusions rules the family out: a COVER_SURFACE rules out PERGOLA, and a NO_COVER_OBSERVED rules out CANOPY and CARPORT, whatever their authority or confidence. A test shows a render-sourced 'sky-render' NO_COVER_OBSERVED excluding CANOPY.
claims.evidence: `const excludedBy = ps.filter((p) => cap.exclusions.includes(p.kind)).map((p) => p.id)`; `expect(open.hypotheses[0].scores.find((s) => s.family === 'CANOPY')?.excludedBy).toEqual(['sky-render'])`
claims.relevance: A low-authority render observation of 'open sky' or 'cover' can veto a technical reading. 005R JSON observations of cover/no-cover must therefore stay out of the proposal stream unless gated.

claims.statement: Pergola vs roof is encoded in four places. (1) PERGOLA requires NO_COVER_OBSERVED and is excluded by COVER_SURFACE. (2) The schema fixes `coverage: z.literal('OPEN')`. (3) The validator raises error PERGOLA_HAS_ROOF when a roof plane, ROOF assembly or roof COVERS or is SUPPORTED_BY a pergola member. (4) The registry text says 'repeated beams are never turned into a roof plane'. A pergola frame without a cover observation stays UNKNOWN with CANOPY/PERGOLA alternatives.
claims.evidence: err('PERGOLA_HAS_ROOF', `... a covered frame is a canopy`). Known gap: 'slatted louvre roofs ... are not distinguished from open pergolas' (capabilities.ts:282).
claims.relevance: Negative semantics for Q4. The louvre gap is a known confusion class for a 005R PERGOLA_OPEN vs COVERED_TERRACE label.

claims.statement: Canopy vs main roof: the canopy cover is emitted as its own ROOF assembly ('<family> cover', classification FLAT/SHED), joined to the host wall by an ABUTMENT edge and ATTACHED_TO. CANOPY outranks ROOF in specificity (2 vs 1). A cover is never invented ('No roof evidence, no roof'). The validator only checks that roofAssemblyId names some ROOF assembly. No rule forbids a canopy from pointing at the main roof assembly.
claims.evidence: `if (!coverP ...) return { ok: false, reason: 'a covered frame without an observed cover' }`; `ref('roofAssemblyId', a.roofAssemblyId, ['assembly'], assemblyOfKind(['ROOF']))`
claims.relevance: Q4: the canopy-vs-main-roof negative is structural (a separate assembly), not validated. A 005R CANOPY_ENTRANCE label has no checked rule against 'main roof eave overhang'.

claims.statement: Balcony vs terrace vs loggia is read from geometry by readPlatformSemantics. Inside a wall ring at or above the platform's level reads LOGGIA. Otherwise more than 1.5 m above the lowest floor reads BALCONY, less than 0.6 m reads TERRACE, and anything between is UNKNOWN. A contradiction is only a WARNING (ASSEMBLY_KIND_CONTRADICTED). Separately, a TERRACE assembly whose platform is a balcony record of another kind is a reference error.
claims.evidence: `if (height > 1.5) return { reading: 'BALCONY' ...}`; `if (height < 0.6) return { reading: 'TERRACE' ...}`; `warn('ASSEMBLY_KIND_CONTRADICTED', ...)`
claims.relevance: These rules need metric heights and a wall ring, which a render JSON cannot provide. 005R BALCONY/LOGGIA/TERRACE labels from images stay visual hypotheses.

claims.statement: Parapet vs railing: a Parapet is a wallPanel with role PARAPET, SUPPORTED_BY the roof plane ('not a slab border'). A railing is a separate `railing` record with role GUARD | HANDRAIL | BALUSTRADE and infill GLASS | BARS | NONE. No validator compares the two. The analyzer still represents a parapet as a raised fascia band.
claims.evidence: Schema enums and the registry knownGaps entry 'the analyzer still represents a parapet as a fascia band raised above a flat roof'.
claims.relevance: Q4 negative: solid-upstand vs open-guard is a type distinction only, with no evidence rule. A render reading 'RAILING' could be a parapet and must abstain.

claims.statement: Open bay vs garage: GARAGE is COMPLETE only with walls and a door. CARPORT is open-sided (openSides), requires posts, and the fusion plausibility check rejects a cover under 12 m². A GarageDoor is a door with usage GARAGE or a PANEL-only assembly. Neither GARAGE nor GARAGE_DOOR has a capability key or a pipeline family.
claims.evidence: `requireFor(a.wallIds.length > 0 && a.doorIds.length > 0)`; `const CARPORT_MIN_COVER_M2 = 12`; `const garage = d.usage === 'GARAGE' || (panels.length > 0 && panels.every((p) => p.kind === 'PANEL'))`
claims.relevance: Q4 negative semantics. The 12 m² threshold is metric, so it cannot be applied from a render.

claims.statement: UnknownArchitecturalAssembly is the safe fallback. It requires sourceEvidenceIds (at least 1), metricExtent, approximateTopology (VOLUME, PLANAR, LINEAR, POINT_CLUSTER or UNKNOWN), observedPlanesOrSegments and unresolvedReason, with optional alternatives {kind, confidence, why}. It may never be COMPLETE. The compiler draws only the observed pieces.
claims.evidence: `if (a.quality === 'COMPLETE') err('ASSEMBLY_QUALITY_OVERSTATED', ... unknown assembly ... cannot be complete`
claims.relevance: Model for the 005R UNKNOWN_ASSEMBLY row and for a per-observation `alternatives` list. The JSON should reuse AssemblyAlternative's shape ({kind, confidence, why}) by reference, not replace it.

claims.statement: The production analyzer v2 (reconstruction) has its own provenance vocabulary: SOURCE_EXACT, SOURCE_CORROBORATED, SOURCE_DERIVED, IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED, VISUAL_SEMANTIC, ASSUMED_FOR_RENDERING, UNRESOLVED. When written to the model, both IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED and VISUAL_SEMANTIC become VISUAL_INFERRED. VISUAL_SEMANTIC features are capped at quality L1.
claims.evidence: `case 'IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED': return 'VISUAL_INFERRED'`; `if (c.printed || c.independentAssets >= 2) return feature.provenance === 'VISUAL_SEMANTIC' ? 'L1' : 'L2'`
claims.relevance: Q3: in production, a render or raster-derived fact reaches the model as VISUAL_INFERRED. 005R JSON could reuse VISUAL_SEMANTIC (class reading) vs IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED (registered measurement) as link values.

claims.statement: In the reference run, a BALCONY feature was solved from an ELEVATION raster 'fascia band' plus a PLAN sighting, with provenance IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED and quality L2 (2 independent assets, nothing printed). The doc calls that ELEVATION asset 'the front render'.
claims.evidence: 'On the front render the fascia reader finds a dark band ...'. The sighting has viewFamily 'ELEVATION'. The feature has provenance 'IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED', quality 'L2'. The reference run lists 10 IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED features.
claims.relevance: Raster-derived exterior metrics already exist in production for balcony, roof pitch, chimney height and verge depth (reconstruction emit.ts:367, :420, :461). The render-vs-technical-elevation naming is already blurred, which is exactly what the 005R router has to decide.

claims.statement: The v2 SourceSighting is the closest existing source-linked image observation type: {id, frameId, assetId, viewFamily, observationIds, pixelRect?, what, confidence}. ViewFamily is PLAN | ELEVATION | SECTION | PERSPECTIVE | SITE | PAGE, with no interior/exterior and no photo/render distinction. FeatureFamilySchema has 22 entries (including TERRACE, BALCONY, RAILING, OPENING) and no PERGOLA, CANOPY, CARPORT, COLUMN or EXTERIOR_STEPS. The doc says '21 families' and is stale by one.
claims.evidence: `ViewFamilySchema = z.enum(['PLAN', 'ELEVATION', 'SECTION', 'PERSPECTIVE', 'SITE', 'PAGE'])`; `PixelRectSchema = z.object({ x0, y0, x1, y1 })`
claims.relevance: 005R router classes (EXTERIOR_RENDER, INTERIOR_RENDER, EXTERIOR_PHOTO, INTERIOR_PHOTO, DETAIL, OTHER, UNKNOWN) are finer than ViewFamily. The JSON should map to ViewFamily as a link field (EXTERIOR_RENDER → PERSPECTIVE, etc.) rather than replace it.

claims.statement: When the pipeline emits, it maps authority to an evidence-source kind: PERSPECTIVE → RENDER, VISUAL_INFERENCE → OTHER, PRINTED/TECHNICAL → DRAWING, CROSS_VIEW/CONVENTION → DERIVATION, and OWNER → MANUAL. The model's EvidenceSource.kind enum is DRAWING | PHOTO | RENDER | PUBLISHED_FACT | MANUAL | DERIVATION | OTHER. PHOTO exists in the model, but no authority maps to it.
claims.evidence: `const SOURCE_KIND: Record<SourceAuthority, 'DRAWING' | 'RENDER' | 'OTHER' | 'DERIVATION'>`
claims.relevance: Link target for the 005R `source.kind`. The photo vs render distinction exists only at EvidenceSource level, not in authority.

claims.statement: The compiler can position the following in 3D: linear solids (column, post, beam, pergola members), balconies, railings, terraces, roof planes, wall panels (parapets), platforms (landing/porch), step runs, windows/doors as fills in wall cuts, and unknown assemblies (observed pieces only). Assemblies own no geometry.
claims.evidence: compileLinearSolid, compileBalcony, compileRailing, compileTerrace, compileRoofPlane, compileWallPanel, compilePlatform, compileStepRun, compileUnknownAssembly.
claims.relevance: 'Can be compiled' column. Every one of these takes metric model records, never an image observation.

claims.statement: In this scope the only real-source (non-synthetic) exterior emitters are in reconstruction v2: createBalcony, createRailing, createTerrace, and a GARAGE_DOOR opening placed as a PANEL door. The railing emitter hard-codes infill 'GLASS' and postSpacing 1.0. No production code emits pergola, canopy, carport, column-as-assembly or exterior-step assemblies.
claims.evidence: `push({ type: 'createRailing', ..., postSpacing: 1.0, infill: 'GLASS', ...})`. A grep for createPergola, createColumn, createBeam, createPlatform, createStepRun and createAssembly in reconstruction, source-vision, source-analyzer and analysis-service found only these three create* calls.
claims.relevance: 'Real-image recognizer exists?' column. Railing infill is a convention, not an observation, so a 005R RAILING observation of infill type has nothing to agree or disagree with.

claims.statement: PORCH exists only as a platform role (LANDING | PORCH | RAMP | PLINTH | UNKNOWN_PLATFORM), listed as primitive 'Landing'. There is no PORCH assembly kind: a porch is an ENTRANCE assembly over a PORCH platform. The demo named 'porch-columns-beams' is actually a CANOPY demonstration.
claims.evidence: `role: z.enum(['LANDING', 'PORCH', 'RAMP', 'PLINTH', 'UNKNOWN_PLATFORM'])`
claims.relevance: PORCH row. In the 005R taxonomy, PORCH should be expressed as a combination (landing + steps + canopy), not as a new assembly kind.

claims.statement: COVERED_TERRACE is representable only as CANOPY with usage TERRACE_COVER. No emitter sets TERRACE_COVER (emitFrame chooses SHELTER, ENTRANCE or UNKNOWN), and no fixture uses it.
claims.evidence: `const usage = family === 'CANOPY' ? (!host ? 'SHELTER' : door ? 'ENTRANCE' : 'UNKNOWN') : undefined`. Grepping for TERRACE_COVER finds only schema.ts:1017.
claims.relevance: COVERED_TERRACE row: the schema has the value, but there is no fixture, demo or recognizer.

claims.statement: The architecture package is held to generality guards: no project names or publisher ids, no known project dimensions, no imports of research/reference/benchmark/stage material, no geometry imports, and no triangles in the hypotheses code.
claims.evidence: Forbidden terms are 'marcow', 'marców', 'rarytas', 'm84f2903cb8e14' and 'archon'. The test also blocks imports matching research/ and stage-reports.
claims.relevance: Any 005R research code must stay out of packages/architecture/src, or these guards will (correctly) fail. Research JSON belongs under research/ and must not be imported by production.

claims.statement: The cleanest non-invasive link schema for a 005R observation is an envelope that carries: source (assetId, frameId, page URL/revision, EvidenceSource.kind), router class (mapped to ViewFamily), pixelRect, assembly label (005R taxonomy) with alternatives in AssemblyAlternative shape, an abstention flag, and optional links (proposalIds/featureKey, SourceSighting id). Metric fields would be forbidden whenever router class is EXTERIOR_RENDER or *_PHOTO.
claims.evidence: Derived from C07, C08, C24, C26 and C27.
claims.relevance: To test: validate a draft research schema whose link fields reference these existing types by id only, and confirm no change to the strict SemanticProposalSchema is needed.

result.notes:
The main points for the 005R stage:

1. **Nothing here recognises real images.** The architecture package's recognition statuses are ANALYZER_V2, SYNTHETIC_PIPELINE or NONE, and the package is unreachable from production. A test enforces that (tests/architecture/assemblies.test.ts:115-125). No code path lets an image observation create or modify an assembly through it.

2. **Production analyzer v2 already reads exterior facts from raster images.** It reads balconies, roof pitch, chimney height and verge depth from elevation and render rasters, records them as IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED, and writes them to the model as VISUAL_INFERRED. The docs call an ELEVATION asset 'the front render', so the line between render and technical elevation is already blurred in production.

3. **BuildApp is looser than the project rule on perspective images.** Its authority ladder allows PERSPECTIVE metric values, at a 0.25 m default tolerance, whenever nothing higher states the quantity. The stricter rule in /home/user/BuildPlan-PC-Legacy/CLAUDE.md:451-453 says a perspective image sets no dimension. 005R should apply the stricter rule in its JSON and report the divergence; it should not change production.

4. **Two pipeline risks to test, not fix.**
   - Exclusions ignore authority (fuse.ts:92), so a render 'no cover' or 'cover' observation can veto a technical reading.
   - PERSPECTIVE is not counted as visual-only, so a single-render pergola may be ACCEPTED (C15, a hypothesis). Its assembly evidence is hard-coded to CROSS_VIEW, giving GEOMETRIC_INFERRED (C16).

5. **What the research JSON can and cannot link to.**
   - SemanticProposal is strict and holds only metre-space geometry, so it cannot carry pixel boxes, asset ids or project revisions.
   - The JSON should be its own envelope that links to SemanticProposal ids, featureKey, the v2 SourceSighting id or pixelRect, ViewFamily, EvidenceSource.kind and AssemblyAlternative.

6. **Gaps in the 005R taxonomy.**
   - There are no capability keys for WINDOW, EXTERIOR_DOOR, GARAGE_DOOR, RAILING, COVERED_TERRACE, PORCH or GARAGE.
   - COVERED_TERRACE exists only as the never-emitted CANOPY usage TERRACE_COVER.
   - PORCH exists only as a platform role.

7. **Doc drift.** FEATURE_IDENTITY_GRAPH.md says 21 feature families; the schema has 22 (TERRACE was added).

8. **Outside my scope but should be audited elsewhere:** packages/source-vision exports a remote Anthropic VLM provider (packages/source-vision/src/index.ts:8).

result.notes:
All five R1 stage reports and all named architecture and 005M-VR2 artifacts exist and were read, with the partial reads listed under missing. The Work OSS report is NOT_AVAILABLE: no in-repo hit, and the 005R contract line 28 requires saying so.

Constraints the 005R stage most needs to keep:
- No VLM adoption without 005M's reopen conditions (OWNER GPU, a frozen real set of ≥ 598–765 questions per class, a crop-decidable generator, a teacher that passes the pair screen).
- Image-derived values are VISUAL_INFERRED only. They never set a dimension, a face or a SOURCE_* status, and one picture is one source.
- Independence is counted by content lineage. No near-duplicate check exists today.
- A no-image (plan-only) baseline arm must come first (005Q recommendation §3).
- No holdout draw. Blind rounds 9–12 are development rows, and Rarytasy is never a blind draw.
- The OWNER APK versionCode 1212 and owner-preview-latest stay untouched.
- The freeze manifest stays IDENTICAL, and no publisher pixel goes into git or to a remote model. The latent remote vision path at source-vision anthropic.ts:88 must stay off.

Three gaps 005R should name:
1. No shipping vocabulary exists for INTERIOR_RENDER, EXTERIOR_PHOTO or INTERIOR_PHOTO (DocumentRoleSchema, ViewFamily), so the router taxonomy must be research-only JSON.
2. Production truth for terraces is partly fabricated, and COVERED_TERRACE is an unreliable plan label, so neither can be used as ground truth.
3. Every prior VLM measurement is on plan crops. Render, photo and interior performance is unmeasured, so 005M numbers must not be extrapolated to them.

No pixel-based role classification exists. The DocumentRole enum has no INTERIOR_RENDER, EXTERIOR_PHOTO, INTERIOR_PHOTO or OTHER: every visualisation is PERSPECTIVE_RENDER.

claims.statement: The vision pass runs once per asset per task that matches the asset's document role. FACADE_DECOMPOSITION covers ELEVATION and PERSPECTIVE_RENDER, PLAN_INTERPRETATION covers FLOOR_PLAN, SECTION_INTERPRETATION covers SECTION. No task exists for SITE_PLAN, DETAIL, CHROME or UNKNOWN, and none for classifying an image.

claims.relevance: The vision reasoner DOES see renders (when a provider is configured), but only to decompose a facade, never to classify or route.

No local or on-device vision model provider exists.

'claude-opus-5'`. The SDK is an optional peerDependency, and node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk exists in this checkout.

claims.statement: The vision reasoner sits behind a flag. The Android/local analyzer has no vision provider, and an architecture test enforces that. analysis-service defaults to nullVisionReasoner. Only the analyzer HTTP API with ANALYZER_VISION=live wires the remote Anthropic provider, with the key read from the server environment.

claims.relevance: In the product path (APK) and in default server runs, nothing visual beyond deterministic CV runs.

claims.statement: The existing holdout graphs ran with no vision. Their gaps record a vision pass NOT_ATTEMPTED for every facade, plan and section asset.
claims.evidence: pod-milorzebem: 19 unresolved entries mention vision, e.g. reason 'no provider could answer (NO_PROVIDER): no vision provider is configured'. marcowki: 18, reason 'no vision provider was configured for this run, so only the deterministic extractors were applied'. Neither graph declares a VISION_MODEL extractor.
claims.relevance: No recorded VLM observation of a real drawing exists to compare against. VISION_REASONER.md:128-134 confirms the fixtures are deliberately synthetic only.

claims.statement: Vision outputs get the extractor kind VISION_MODEL, the provider/model/task name and version, the model's self-reported confidence, and a positional uncertainty floored at 1 px. They are added ALONGSIDE the CV observations and never replace them. A rejected answer is discarded whole and recorded as a MISSING gap.
claims.evidence: analyze.ts:199 `declare(extractorNameFor(provider, task), extractorVersionFor(provider), 'VISION_MODEL')`. apply.ts:69 `Math.max(MIN_VISION_POSITION_PX, round6(stated))`. apply.ts:79 confidence: o.confidence, used as given.
claims.relevance: Vision has no elevated authority. Its confidence is uncalibrated and taken at face value.

claims.statement: A vision output cannot change an asset's role. The role is an INPUT to the request and to the prompt. The response schema is .strict() and has no roles field. The frame is declared from SourcePackage roles before vision runs, and applyVisionResponse writes onto the caller-supplied frame and refuses a byte-hash mismatch.
claims.evidence: anthropic.ts:88 prompt line: 'The publisher classifies this drawing as: document=${request.roles.document}, ...'. The model can disagree only in free-text notes (sent to traces, analyze.ts:203-207) or notFound (becomes MISSING gaps, apply.ts:102).
claims.relevance: This satisfies 'must not silently override roles', but the VLM is also primed with the possibly-wrong role and has no structured way to dispute it.

claims.statement: A vision output cannot create geometry: it can only produce 2D observations on the image. Architecture tests check that the vision response schema names no DSL/metre/mesh terms. Validation refuses kinds outside the task vocabulary and refuses cross-view identity relations.
claims.evidence: validate.ts:95 KIND_NOT_ALLOWED. validate.ts:103 RELATION_NOT_ALLOWED. analyzer.test.ts:145 'offers a vision provider no way to return anything but observations'.

claims.statement: Downstream, reconstruction v2 marks observations on PERSPECTIVE frames as LOW authority. They are USED_AS_CORROBORATION only when a camera was solved for that render, otherwise IGNORED_WITH_REASON. Among leftover observations, OPENING/LOGGIA corroborate only on the ELEVATION view family, and the kinds WINDOW, DOOR, BALCONY and RAILING have no branch, so they fall to the default IGNORED_WITH_REASON.

'USED_AS_CORROBORATION' : 'IGNORED_WITH_REASON'). reconstruct-v2.ts:1414-1415 default disposition 'IGNORED_WITH_REASON', 'read for the record; the v2 passes read this drawing's pixels directly'. run.ts:155 comment: 'A render is a picture of the house, not a drawing of it' (TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTS excludes PERSPECTIVE_RENDER).

claims.statement: Deterministic CV never emits WINDOW, DOOR, BALCONY, RAILING or CHIMNEY. On elevations and renders it emits only SILHOUETTE, MASS_REGION, ROOF_EDGE, RIDGE, LOGGIA, OPENING, LINEAR_VOLUME_CANDIDATE (hints beam/column/side-return), WALL_REGION (side-return) and SURFACE_REGION. Those five semantic kinds can come only from a vision task.
claims.evidence: Every builder.observe kind in elevation.ts is listed above. The R4-04 measured counts contain no WINDOW/DOOR/BALCONY/RAILING in any graph.
claims.relevance: Today no window/door distinction exists, and the observation graph has no railing/balcony recognition from real images.

claims.statement: Each observation links to its source by assetId, variantByteHash (SHA-256 of the exact bytes), frameId, pixelGeometry (POINT/SEGMENT/POLYLINE/POLYGON/RECT/LINE_FAMILY in decoded pixels) and a derived normGeometry. The validator refuses mismatched frame/asset/bytes, out-of-bounds coordinates, and non-derived ids.
claims.evidence: SourceObservationSchema fields assetId, variantByteHash (/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/), frameId, pixelGeometry, normGeometry, confidence, uncertainty{positionPx}, provenance, alternatives.
claims.relevance: This source-linking pattern (asset id + byte hash + pixel box + uncertainty + alternatives) should be reused by the 005R JSON.

claims.statement: Graph frames carry a COPY of the SourcePackage roles 'so the graph can be read without the package beside it'. The frame id is derived from assetId and variantByteHash only, not from roles, and validateObservationGraph never reads frame.roles. Nothing checks that a graph's frame roles match the package's.
claims.evidence: A grep for 'roles' in validate.ts finds no hits. frameId = stableId('frame', assetId, { assetId, variantByteHash }).
claims.relevance: Divergent roles in a graph would not be caught structurally. A router writing roles anywhere graph-adjacent must be a separate, named claim.

claims.statement: The observation graph has no observation kind that classifies a whole asset (no 'this image is an interior render'), and no field for project version or edition beyond sourcePackageId and sourcePackageHash.
claims.evidence: SourceObservationGraphSchema top-level fields: schema, schemaVersion, id, sourcePackageId, sourcePackageHash, extractors, coordinateFrames, observations, relations, conflicts, unresolved, contentHash.
claims.relevance: Router output (an asset class with uncertainty) has no home in either typed JSON. It needs a separate research artifact keyed by assetId plus variantByteHash plus sourcePackageHash.

claims.statement: Real-image exterior recognition on technical elevations happens today in reconstruction v2, which reads registered elevation rasters directly, not through the observation graph. Opening sill and head come from verticalOpeningExtent, a differential column-band test. The opening family (WINDOW/DOOR/GARAGE_DOOR/...) comes from the plan symbol and proportions. Balcony fascia and railing come from readFasciaBand/readRailing on upper-storey recesses, and terraces from plan recess zones plus a plan outline.

The family is a reading of the plan symbol and the proportions, never of the sill alone.' OpeningFamily = 'WINDOW'|'DOOR'|'GARAGE_DOOR'|'GLAZED_DOOR'|'MULTI_PANEL_GLAZING'|'UNKNOWN'.
claims.relevance: Exterior recognition on elevations exists, but it is plan-anchored and metric. It is not an independent image classifier and does not run on renders.

claims.statement: No real-image recognition of exterior features on renders exists. The only render-specific processing is perspective camera resection from silhouette corners against the already-reconstructed envelope. Render observations then serve as depth-order corroboration only.
claims.evidence: solvePerspectiveCamera(raster, frame.id, { envelope, eaveY, ridgeY, ... }). Observations on the frame are recorded with authority 'LOW' and disposition 'the perspective is registered; depth order was checked against it'.
claims.relevance: Expected finding confirmed: render recognition of pergola, canopy, terrace, railing and so on is absent.

claims.statement: SemanticProposal in packages/architecture already has detector 'VLM' and kinds that cover exterior assemblies: VERTICAL_MEMBER (post/column), HORIZONTAL_MEMBER (pergola beam), COVER_SURFACE (canopy plate), NO_COVER_OBSERVED (sky between members), STEP_EDGE and LEVEL_SURFACE (terrace). Its geometry is world-coordinate Vec3 with only sourceFrameId, with no assetId, byte hash or pixel box. No production package or app imports it, only tests.

claims.relevance: Existing architectural language for pergola/canopy/terrace evidence, but it is metric and not pixel-linked, so it cannot hold raw image observations.

claims.statement: Debug overlays embed the source image as a data URI in the SVG.
claims.evidence: 'The image is embedded as a data URI so an overlay is one self-contained file that survives being copied out of the repository.'
claims.relevance: Safety for 005R: any overlay generated during research carries publisher pixels and must not be committed or sent to a remote model.

claims.statement: A cheap, local, deterministic router signal set already exists in-repo: drawingCharacter tone share (R4-07) and the elevation extractor's silhouette/mass coverage. Combined, they would separate line drawings (plan/elevation/section) from renders and photos with high precision. Separating EXTERIOR from INTERIOR renders, and photos from renders, has no existing signal.

result.notes:
Main conclusions for 005R:
(a) Renders are not skipped. They go through facade CV and produce many OPENING, LOGGIA and LINEAR_VOLUME_CANDIDATE observations, which the repository's own metrology doc says are not real windows. Treat them as a known-bad V0 baseline.
(b) The only VLM path is the remote Anthropic provider. It sits behind ANALYZER_VISION=live on the server API and is absent from the APK. It sends raw publisher pixels off-machine, so it is not admissible as a 005R local candidate under the stage rules.
(c) Neither SourcePackage nor SourceObservationGraph has slots for the 005R classes:
- interior vs exterior render, photo, OTHER
- pergola, canopy, carport, terrace, garage door, exterior steps
The 005R JSON should be a separate research artifact, keyed by sourcePackageHash + assetId + variantByteHash + pixel rect. It should copy the graph's confidence / uncertainty / alternatives / unresolved pattern and never write roles back.
(d) Exterior recognition that works today lives in reconstruction v2 and is plan-anchored and metric (openings-v2, readFasciaBand, readRailing). It is not image classification.
(e) packages/architecture SemanticProposal already names VLM-detector kinds for posts, beams, cover/no-cover and step edges. It is world-metric with no pixel provenance and is unused in production.
Scratch script used for counting (text JSON only): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/5eccf0e3-4ef3-5405-aafb-08cd5094f39b/scratchpad/graphstats.py. No repository file was modified.

claims.statement: Variant identity is the SHA-256 of the bytes (byteHash). Variant id = stableId('var', filename, {byteHash}). Within an asset the variants are ordered by decoded pixel area, then byteLength, then byteHash. selectedVariantId = ordered[0]. selectionReason is prose and is excluded from the hash. Dimensions come only from probeImage on the bytes; declared HTML sizes are recorded as declaredMismatch.

claims.statement: Grouping in the real pipeline is union-find over (adapter groupKey | discovery groupKey | identical byteHash). Exact byte duplicates within a package collapse to one variant with a BYTE_IDENTICAL failure naming the dropped address. The 'group by roles plus aspect' function groupVariants (and the SourceAssetSchema comment describing it) is used only in tests, not by acquire.ts.

claims.statement: Roles are evidenced claims. Each RoleClaim carries {signal, detail, confidence}. mergeRoleClaims takes the highest confidence per dimension. result.notes:
Five findings matter most for 005R's design.

1. No router category exists today. INTERIOR, EXTERIOR and PHOTO appear nowhere in the schema; every visualisation is PERSPECTIVE_RENDER. The ARCHON adapter never reads data-fancybox-position, and the architecture test (tests/architecture/analyzer.test.ts:239-256) forbids 'fancybox' outside src/adapters and inside the generic adapter. A fancybox3Interiors signal would therefore have to live in adapters/archon.ts as an additional claim, or in a sidecar keyed by (package contentHash, assetId, byteHash). Changing roles moves the content hash and every frame id, because roles are hashed and nothing downstream mutates them.

2. Interior renders are already analysed as exteriors. In rarytasy-g2e, 19 interior frames (living area, kitchen, bathroom) got RIDGE, SILHOUETTE, ROOF_EDGE, OPENING and LOGGIA observations, with about 201 relations attached. This is the strongest measured argument for a router.

3. Caption provenance is lossy. The highest-trust channel (OG_IMAGE) has no caption, so 21/37 g2e assets have caption null. The interior wording survives only in roleEvidence prose, truncated to 80 characters and not hashed. Any caption-based labeling for 005R must read roleEvidence.detail or re-acquire the markup; asset.caption alone is not enough.

4. The generic adapter misreads DobreDomy taglines. 'z poddaszem' gives storey ATTIC, and 'na wąską działkę' gives SITE_PLAN with ORTHOGRAPHIC_PLAN projection. Of 42 render slides across D00–D05, only 6 are PERSPECTIVE_RENDER (one og:image per house, at 0.4). Any 005R corpus that takes current roles as ground truth for DobreDomy is contaminated. Use these as negative controls, not labels.

5. Edition identity. The dev case 'rarytasy-g2e' is m84f2903cb8e14, "Dom w rarytasach 5 (G2E)". It is not the OWNER anchor m3ea28300f9b3e, which appears nowhere in the repo and has no sealed package. e-OZE and 5 (G2E) share 5 byte-identical interior renders, and nothing detects this across packages. A cross-edition byteHash ledger (or perceptual hash) is needed for the negative cross-edition-mixing control the contract requires.

Minor: docs/SOURCE_PACKAGE.md:185-186 contradicts hash.ts on what the hash covers; groupVariants and selectAsset are test-only or unused; the doc header still says schema 1.0.0 while the code is at 1.2.0/1.3.0.

claims.statement: TERRACE_AT_GRADE comes from plan geometry only. Recess floor: a ZONE strip between the walled envelope and the extent the dimension chains state, with a body face on its back plane, at storey 0. Platform: an optional extension where the plan raster shows a thin outline spanning >=85% of the facade, 0.3-5 m out from the mouth, with >=30% drawn-on (hatch or furniture) pixels in between. Provenance is SOURCE_DERIVED. Thickness = floor datum minus a negative terrain datum (LEVEL_DATUM between -1.5 and 0), else an assumed 0.15 m labelled ASSUMED_FOR_RENDERING. Surface is PAVED when an extension exists or drawnShare >= 0.3, else UNKNOWN.

claims.statement: PERGOLA_OPEN is not represented. The boundary readers deliberately exclude pergolas. Glazing between two free posts is read as 'a pergola's or a balustrade's, not a facade's'. A gap beside free-standing blocks is TRUE_EXTERIOR_GAP 'FREE_STANDING_BLOCK'. A pergola, terrace on posts, canopy or line work 'encloses nothing and is never a part'.
claims.evidence: boundary-evidence.ts:621 decide('TRUE_EXTERIOR_GAP','NONE','FREE_STANDING_BLOCK', ...). plan-decomposition.ts:1286 'one wall running on alone is a wing, a fence or a pergola, and is left to the bays'.
claims.relevance: Pergola evidence is actively discarded so the building envelope stays clean.

claims.statement: CANOPY_ENTRANCE / porch exists only as a 'portal head'. That is a band on the FRONT elevation that continues an upper-storey balcony fascia across an ATTACHED body. The body's flat roof must project over the front zone: dark-pixel share > 0.6 along a line near the zone mouth on the top-storey plan. The band must also cover >= 60% of the body's width. Provenance is SOURCE_CORROBORATED. No free-standing entrance canopy, porch roof or porch columns are produced. Open bays (porch, carport) 'stay ground'.
claims.evidence: if (recess.side !== 'FRONT' || portalHeads.some(...)) continue. if (!across || across.to - across.from < (m.x1 - m.x0) * 0.6) continue. projects = n > 0 && dark / n > 0.6.
claims.relevance: A canopy on a house without a balcony fascia above it, or on a side or rear facade, can never be built.

claims.statement: CARPORT is not represented. A carport's open side is read as where the wall stops: maxOpeningM 3.2. A bay with nothing drawn across its mouth stays ground. A recess deeper than 4.5 m is treated as the back of a garage, carport or room.
claims.evidence: maxOpeningM: 3.2 ('the mouth of a loggia and the open side of a carport'). RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M = 4.5.
claims.relevance: Carport roof and posts are absent from 3D.

claims.statement: BALCONY needs four things: a ZONE recess at storey > 0; at least one registered elevation of that facade; readFasciaBand finding a DARK/MID tone band within 0.4 m of the floor level in >= 4 of 6 columns, 0.25-1.2 m tall with spread <= 0.35 m; and fasciaExtent. Kind is always 'BALCONY'. Provenance is IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED, emitted as VISUAL_INFERRED. Along-facade extent comes from elevation pixel columns. Depth (z) comes from the plan zone's mouth and back. Top = min(floor + 0.05, fascia top). Only the first view that yields a fascia is used (break).
claims.evidence: facade.ts:142 'if (reads.length < 4) return undefined'. :147 'if (top - bottom < 0.25 || top - bottom > 1.2) return undefined'. :149 'if (spread > 0.35) return undefined'.
claims.relevance: Balcony detection is a tone-band reader on the elevation, gated by plan topology. A cantilevered balcony outside any dimensioned zone cannot appear.

claims.statement: LOGGIA is not distinguished. The model schema allows BalconyKind 'LOGGIA', but the solver writes 'BALCONY' for every upper recess. A ground-level loggia becomes a terrace. The recess topology (mouth, back, returns) is the loggia's shape.
claims.evidence: balconies.push({ id, kind: 'BALCONY', ... }). Doc: 'A loggia, a set-back entrance and a balcony under the roof are all the same shape of fact'.
claims.relevance: A LOGGIA label from an image router has no distinct consumer.

claims.statement: RAILING is built only on a solved balcony (never on terraces, stairs or roofs). readRailing scans up from slab + 0.12 m for a thin darker line after >= 0.5 m of panel, needs >= 3 of 6 columns, and accepts height 0.5-1.4 m. The emitter hard-codes infill 'GLASS' and postSpacing 1.0, which are neither read nor labelled as assumptions in the command. The plan path (turns) is SOURCE_DERIVED from a drawn line across the zone. Overall provenance is IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED, emitted as VISUAL_INFERRED.
claims.evidence: facade.ts:165 doc says '/** A glass balustrade above a slab ...'. :194 'if (tops.length < 3) return undefined'. :198 'if (height < 0.5 || height > 1.4) return undefined'. emit.ts:435 '... postSpacing: 1.0, infill: 'GLASS' ...'.
claims.relevance: Railing material and posts are assumptions. A railing on a terrace or exterior stair never reaches 3D.

claims.statement: COLUMN_POST is not represented. No createColumn is emitted. Posts on the plan are explicitly refused as jambs ('a post is never a jamb'), and gaps beside them become TRUE_EXTERIOR_GAP. The nearest exterior vertical members are RETURN_WALLs: wall-thick ink across a zone, SOURCE_DERIVED.
claims.evidence: returns.push({ ... provenance: 'SOURCE_DERIVED', why: `a ${r.thicknessM} m return standing in the ... zone` }).
claims.relevance: Porch, carport and pergola posts are invisible to the 3D model.

claims.statement: EXTERIOR_STEPS are not represented. The only stair reader searches tread ladders inside the main body's rectangle and builds one interior stair from level 0 to level 1. If none is found, a MISSING gap is recorded. createStepRun exists in the DSL but is never emitted by reconstruction.
claims.evidence: const body = { x0: main.x0, z0: main.z0, x1: main.x1, z1: main.z1 }; for (const ladder of findTreadLadders(entry.raster, entry.frame, body)).
claims.relevance: Entrance steps and terrace steps drawn outside the body are never searched for.

claims.statement: GARAGE_DOOR is an OpeningV2 family assigned by rule: an ATTACHED single-storey body, storey 0, width >= 2.2 m, and sill within 0.1 m of the floor. The family's provenance is VISUAL_SEMANTIC (emitted as VISUAL_INFERRED). Position and width come from the plan gap, corrected to the printed callout width when one agrees (SOURCE_EXACT width). Height comes from the callout and/or elevation. The emitter places a single PANEL door. The boundary reader separately recognises a VEHICLE_DOOR gap (2.2-3.2 m, line at the wall face, jambs both sides) to close the outline.
claims.evidence: const attachedVehicle = input.attachedSingleStorey && host.storeyIndex === 0 && widthM >= 2.2 && sillY - host.floorY < 0.1.
claims.relevance: A garage door in the main body, or on a two-storey garage, is never typed GARAGE_DOOR.

claims.statement: WINDOW and EXTERIOR_DOOR: interval and position come from plan wall gaps (0.5-6.5 m) on each storey's registered plan. Width comes from a callout like '110/230' within 2 m whose width agrees within max(0.12 m, 12%). Sill and head come from the callout plus the registered elevation (SOURCE_CORROBORATED when they agree within 0.2 m). With an elevation only they are IMAGE_METRIC_REGISTERED. With neither, sill = floor and head = floor + 2.1 m, ASSUMED_FOR_RENDERING. Family comes from proportions plus plan symbols (glazing lines, door swing): DOOR, GLAZED_DOOR, MULTI_PANEL_GLAZING or WINDOW. Family provenance is always VISUAL_SEMANTIC.
claims.evidence: DEFAULTS { minWidthM: 0.5, maxWidthM: 6.5, calloutReachM: 2.0 }. Final else branch: 'sillY = host.floorY; headY = host.floorY + 2.1; prov.sill = prov.head = 'ASSUMED_FOR_RENDERING''.
claims.relevance: Opening positions are measured plan geometry. Elevations add only vertical extents. Renders add nothing.

claims.statement: views.ts (v1 registration, still used by v2 through solve.registerElevationFrames) registers each ORTHOGRAPHIC_ELEVATION frame with one isotropic scale: section total height / pixel height. The extent is the traced SILHOUETTE unless it covers >= 85% of the sheet; otherwise it is measured off the pixels with architecturalBounds. Overhang = half the surplus width.
claims.evidence: DEGENERATE_SILHOUETTE_COVERAGE = 0.85. scale = massing.totalHeight / pixelHeight. overhang = max(0, (widthM - spanM)/2).
claims.relevance: Every elevation reading (balcony, railing, sill/head) depends on this registration.

claims.statement: views.ts side assignment honours a publisher label only for view === 'FRONT'|'REAR'|'LEFT'|'RIGHT'. The source-package enum is FRONT, REAR, SIDE_UNSPECIFIED, SIDE_LEFT, SIDE_RIGHT, so SIDE_LEFT, SIDE_RIGHT and SIDE_UNSPECIFIED all fall to width-based choice. That choice picks the axis whose span the width exceeds least (allowing a shortfall up to max(0.25 m, 4%)). If both walls on that axis are free it takes the first free one at confidence 0.4. If both are taken the view is refused.
claims.evidence: labelled = (frame) => frame.roles.view === 'FRONT' || ... 'LEFT' || ... 'RIGHT'. free.length === 2: 'takes the first free one', confidence 0.4. ARCHON labels both 'boczna' views SIDE_UNSPECIFIED. The generic adapter emits SIDE_LEFT/SIDE_RIGHT.
claims.relevance: Side views are initially assigned by order, not by label.

claims.statement: v2 corrects unlabelled side views after the main roof is solved, using decideSideOrientation. All LEFT/RIGHT views not labelled LEFT/RIGHT/SIDE_LEFT/SIDE_RIGHT are re-registered mirrored. They are swapped only if every readable view (>= 10 samples) fits the main body's top profile better mirrored by >= 0.25 m median. A symmetric profile never swaps.
claims.evidence: MARGIN_M = 0.25. const swap = agree === read. 'A symmetric profile fits both ways equally and never swaps.'
claims.relevance: On symmetric gable houses, SIDE_UNSPECIFIED views keep their coin-toss assignment. Side-facade openings and balconies can then sit at the mirrored end.

claims.statement: A view the generic adapter labels SIDE_LEFT or SIDE_RIGHT is assigned by width order in views.ts (its label is ignored there), and v2 then excludes it from the orientation check because it counts as labelled. The stated side is therefore never enforced and never re-checked. A 'prawa' view could stay on the LEFT wall.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the two predicates using different vocabularies ('LEFT' vs 'SIDE_LEFT'). Not executed.
claims.relevance: Test: a synthetic generic-adapter package with a single 'elewacja prawa' ELEVATION frame. Check that registrations.elevations[].side === 'RIGHT'. The hypothesis predicts LEFT.

claims.statement: Mirroring and handedness: v1 elevationMetric applies no reflection (u = (x - x0)·mpp - overhang), on the stated argument that the drawing's left edge is where the anticlockwise ring wall starts. v2 makes the direction explicit per side: alongSign = +1 for FRONT/RIGHT and -1 for REAR/LEFT, with alongAtLeft chosen per side.
claims.evidence: frame.ts:348 comment: 'FRONT west→east, REAR east→west, LEFT (west wall) rear→front, RIGHT (east wall) front→rear'.
claims.relevance: Any JSON observation in elevation pixels needs this exact convention to land on the right wall end.

claims.statement: v2 needs a ridge datum to use any elevation: legacy registrations with no side are skipped, and if ridgeY is undefined every elevation is skipped. The gap recorded is 'no ridge datum was read from a section'. registerElevationV2 also refuses a view whose ground error is > 0.9 m against the terrain datum or 0.
claims.evidence: if (!frame || !raster || ridgeY === undefined) continue. if (best.err > 0.9) return undefined.
claims.relevance: With no section, balconies, railings, elevation sill/heads, verges and portal heads all vanish together.

claims.statement: Perspective renders (projection PERSPECTIVE, from ARCHON 'widok'/'wizualizacja') feed no geometry. A camera is attempted per render. Solved cameras only produce a CAMERA feature record. Their observations are logged as USED_AS_CORROBORATION (solved) or IGNORED_WITH_REASON (unsolved). LINEAR_VOLUME_CANDIDATEs on unregistered views (perspectives) are IGNORED_WITH_REASON.
claims.evidence: solvedCameras is referenced only at 1165, 1174 and 1179 (the step summary). No terrace, balcony, opening or railing code reads it.
claims.relevance: Renders are unused for exterior assemblies today. Any render-derived observation would be new evidence with no consumer.

claims.statement: The word 'render' in v2 means the ORTHOGRAPHIC_ELEVATION frames, which on ARCHON are photo-realistic. These ARE used for: ridge-axis apex votes, the side-orientation check, verge members, balcony fascias, railings, portal heads, opening sill and head, attached-roof form, chimneys above the roof, rooflights and wall tones.
claims.evidence: Step text 'renders registered on the ridge datum'. The ledger reason calls each elevation 'the ... render'.
claims.relevance: The router must keep 'technical elevation' and 'rendered elevation' as different classes. The pipeline already treats rendered elevations as metric views.

claims.statement: Asset classification today comes from URL-slug and caption keyword rules, not pixels: 'elewacj' -> ELEVATION, 'widok|wizualizacj' -> PERSPECTIVE_RENDER, 'sytuacj' -> SITE_PLAN, 'przekroj' -> SECTION. Projection is derived from the document role. There are no INTERIOR_RENDER or PHOTO classes; the DocumentRole enum is FLOOR_PLAN, SECTION, ELEVATION, SITE_PLAN, PERSPECTIVE_RENDER, DETAIL, CHROME, UNKNOWN.
claims.evidence: { test: /\bwidok\b|\bwizualizacj\w*/, claim: { document: 'PERSPECTIVE_RENDER' } }.
claims.relevance: An interior visualisation captioned 'wizualizacja' is routed as PERSPECTIVE and fed to the camera solver as if it were exterior. This is the router gap 005R studies.

claims.statement: Sealed Marcowki auto-v3 candidate (solver 2.0.0) emits: 2 createTerrace (PAVED/PLINTH, thickness 0.15 ASSUMED); 2 createBalcony (BALCONY, VISUAL_INFERRED); 2 createRailing (GLASS, postSpacing 1, heights 0.910 and 0.924, VISUAL_INFERRED); 9 windows; 12 doors, of which 1 is a PANEL garage door. Auto-v2 had the terraces as createBalcony kind TERRACE (thickness 0.2).
claims.evidence: program command counts: createTerrace 2, createBalcony 2, createRailing 2, placeWindow 9, placeDoor 12. setEvidence terrace-front-66 status SOURCE_DERIVED, properties.thickness 'ASSUMED'. Garage opening opening-0-front-8-0 interpretation 'a 2.72 m gap ... printed 275/275, not read on an elevation', kind 'VISUAL_INFERRED', height 'UNRESOLVED'.
claims.relevance: Confirms the provenance labels predicted by code on the one house with sealed output.

claims.statement: On real ARCHON holdout runs the pipeline produced terraces but no balconies or railings. Azaliach 3: terraces 3, balconies 0, railings 0, openings 6, with 5 PERSPECTIVE_RENDER and 4 ELEVATION assets. Tunbergiach 7 R2: terraces 2, balconies 0, railings 0, openings 8. Rarytasy: terraces 2, balconies 0, railings 0, openings 14.

claims.relevance: The terrace/balcony/railing counts above are from these artifacts.

claims.statement: Azaliach 3 (005C artifact) has terrace-front-0, a 10.55 m x 0.218 m strip, and terrace-rear-0, 10.55 x 1.07 m, both PAVED with a plinth.
claims.relevance: Shows any dimensioned zone strip becomes a 'terrace'.

claims.statement: The 0.22 m Azaliach 'terrace' is a dimension-extent or wall-finish strip, not a real terrace. It was produced before the 005Q wall-strip rule (isWallStripZone), which may or may not suppress it at HEAD.
claims.evidence: Inference from geometry (thinner than a step) and artifact date versus the 005Q change.
claims.relevance: Test: re-run Azaliach at HEAD and inspect terraces[] plus the gap 'outer-face-zone-max_z'. Compare against the ARCHON plan by a human label, not a model.

claims.statement: Docs describe a 'linear solid evidence gate' in which a perspective depth cue can support a facade band (condition B). In v2 no code path consumes perspective depth cues: cameras are recorded only, and stripes are accepted only when they hit a member on a registered elevation view.

result.notes:
The anchor files' line numbers are cited above. Six findings bear most on 005R:

(a) Exterior assemblies are created almost entirely from plan topology. Dimensioned ZONE strips become recesses, which become terraces, balconies and returns. Rendered orthographic elevations only confirm or size bands (fascia, railing, sill/head). Perspective renders and room-name tables contribute nothing to geometry.

(b) Pergola, carport, entrance canopy (except the portal-head case), column/post and exterior steps cannot reach 3D at all. The model schema has types for them (CANOPY, PERGOLA, CARPORT, EXTERIOR_STAIR, createColumn, createStepRun), but only packages/architecture uses them, and the real pipeline does not depend on it.

(c) Asset routing today is URL/caption keyword rules (archon.ts:95-99). There is no INTERIOR_RENDER or PHOTO role, so an interior 'wizualizacja' would be routed as a PERSPECTIVE exterior candidate. Only the camera solver consumes that route, and it emits nothing geometric.

(d) Several values look measured but are conventions: railing infill GLASS and postSpacing 1.0, terrace thickness 0.15 m, door head floor + 2.1 m. The first is not labelled as an assumption in the command, though thickness and sill/head do carry ASSUMED labels in setEvidence.

result.notes: Summary for the orchestrator. (1) Rarytasy-like exterior parts are lost at several independent points, not at one stage. The publisher's prose is never parsed for terrace, pergola or canopy (specifications.ts reads the roof only). The reconstruction has no producer for PERGOLA, CANOPY or CARPORT; the architecture package that can emit them is not a dependency. Terraces exist only as recess floors, so a flat garden facade gets no terrace. The stripe rule rejects every elevation linear volume unless a verge or balcony fascia member exists, and on single-storey ridge-X houses no such member can exist. (2) The pipeline also fabricates: a dimensioned zone with zero returns becomes a 'recess' and then a terrace (g2e's 55.7 m² over open ground, which 005Q already recorded). A failed elevation registration silently means 'roof does not cover zones' (jarząbem). (3) The incumbent router puts interior renders in the same PERSPECTIVE_RENDER role as exterior ones (archon.ts:98; schema.ts:45 has no such dimension). On G2E-5, 19 of 25 perspective frames are interior. They go through the exterior CV extractors (analyze.ts:164) and get camera solves. 12 cameras were solved with only 6 exterior frames available, so at least 6 interior solves are likely (HYPOTHESIS R6-18). No perspective render contributes geometry to any model. 'Render' in model evidence strings means an orthographic elevation. (4) Edition hygiene: rarytasy-g2e is G2E-5 (m84f…) and is not the OWNER anchor (m3ea…). By room table, rarytasy-eoze is closer to the anchor house. No output exists for the anchor itself. Historical reports call G2E-5 the owner's project, so findings must be tagged by edition. Recommendation inside this scope: Task B ground truth for the anchor must come from anchor-edition assets only. The exterior JSON should carry the edition code per observation. Router evaluation should count interior-render false routes, since the incumbent conflates them. Do not treat rarytasy-g2e outputs as anchor evidence.

result.notes:
How to read this:
- HEAD on disk is 0d02e53 (005R freeze-manifest commit). 39061db is its parent and an ancestor of HEAD. The worktree is not clean: there are untracked 005R harness files, which belong to the parent stage and which I did not read.
- I did not run or check CI for this scope.

Most load-bearing findings for 005R design:
1. Neither "observations cannot silently override roles" nor "roles are not pixel truth" is stated anywhere I read. Role claims come only from text and filenames (R8-11, R8-12, R8-36). 005R should write these rules into its preregistration and schema, and model a role/pixel disagreement as a CONFLICT record.
2. The package role vocabulary cannot express INTERIOR_RENDER, EXTERIOR_PHOTO, INTERIOR_PHOTO or TECHNICAL_ELEVATION (R8-13). The 005R taxonomy is research-only JSON until an authorised schema stage.
3. Doctrine forbids SOURCE_EXACT, SOURCE_CORROBORATED and SOURCE_DERIVED for render-derived values. Class observations are VISUAL_SEMANTIC (L1 cap) and become VISUAL_INFERRED in the model (R8-04, R8-05, R8-33).
4. COVERED_TERRACE collides with a production plan BodyRelation (R8-19).
5. A remote vision adapter exists (anthropicVisionReasoner, R8-10). It must not be used, given the no-publisher-pixels-to-remote rule.
6. Prior stages already show small VLMs at 30.9% confident-wrong and a synthetic-trained whole-image classifier collapsing from 85% to 49.6% on real data (R8-30). This is the in-repo evidence behind "do not adopt a model because of selected examples".
7. Per 005Q, production recognition of CANOPY, PERGOLA, CARPORT, COLUMN and ENTRANCE is 0 on 24 models, and 17 of 29 plan terraces are slivers (R8-18). The no-image baseline for those classes is effectively empty, and plan terraces are not usable as truth.

Supplementary files outside the listed R8 set were read only where Q2 and Q5 required it (SOURCE_PACKAGE, VISION_REASONER, SOURCE_OBSERVATION_GRAPH, ARCHITECTURAL_LANGUAGE, the 005Q interface artifact).

verdicts.correction: Verified. capabilities.ts:24 has RecognitionStatus = 'ANALYZER_V2' | 'SYNTHETIC_PIPELINE' | 'NONE'. CAPABILITY_KEYS at :26-48 has 21 keys. The header at :10-15 contains the quoted sentence.

I parsed the JSON again. The top-level keys are [assemblies, capabilities, primitives, relationships, schema, schemaVersion], and there are 21 capabilities. TERRACE and BALCONY are SUPPORTED/ANALYZER_V2. CANOPY, PERGOLA, COLUMN, BEAM, EXTERIOR_STEPS, ENTRANCE and UNKNOWN_ASSEMBLY are SUPPORTED/SYNTHETIC_PIPELINE. CARPORT is SUPPORTED/NONE, LOGGIA PARTIAL/NONE, HANDRAIL PARTIAL/NONE, PARAPET SUPPORTED/NONE. The recognition lines in the source (:93…:351) are in the same order.

True for the capability registry. Qualification: outside the registry, production reconstruction v2 does classify WINDOW, DOOR, GARAGE_DOOR, GLAZED_DOOR and MULTI_PANEL_GLAZING openings (packages/reconstruction/src/v2/openings-v2.ts:23) and emits them (emit.ts:491-498). So 'no capability entry' must not be read as 'no real-source recognition' for windows, doors or garage doors.

FAMILIES (types.ts:12) and EMITTERS (emit.ts:686-693) are correct. 'Can only end up as UNKNOWN' is overstated. Evidence for these classes can also be REJECTED (fuse.ts:148-149, nothing emitted), or mis-ACCEPTED as one of the six families. For example, a LEVEL_SURFACE plus STEP_EDGEs can satisfy EXTERIOR_STEPS, and a covered terrace with COVER_SURFACE can satisfy CANOPY. 'OPENING evidence for ENTRANCE' is also wrong. ENTRANCE is not a pipeline family: it is absent from CAPABILITY_OF at fuse.ts:32-40, so its OPENING requirement (capabilities.ts:328) is never scored. The entrance door comes from the context model's doors and openings (emit.ts:532, ~616-630), not from an OPENING proposal. An OPENING proposal is consumed only by the dormer emitter (emit.ts:312).

The conclusion holds by grep (MEASURED): the only *.ts/*.tsx/*.js importer of @buildapp/architecture outside its own package is packages/editor/test/categories.test.ts plus tests/architecture. Two parts are overstated. (1) The test does not enforce this for all production code. Its list (assemblies.test.ts:117-120) leaves out source-vision, image-metrology, verification, candidates, evidence-pack, source-common, numeric-recogniser-ort and apps/android. Its importsOf regex (:38-41) catches only static import/export statements, not dynamic import(). (2) tests/architecture/package.json:2 also contains the string ('@buildapp/architecture-tests'), so 'only packages/architecture/package.json:2' is inexact, though that entry is a package name, not a dependency.

Verified. proposals.ts:1-12 says 'no detector writes the model'. pipeline.ts:14-16 says it 'reads its context model and writes nothing'. types.ts:74 says 'It is read, never written.' The test at assemblies.test.ts:102-112 checks every command against BuildingCommandSchema. Note: runPipeline itself does not apply the commands. Only applyPipeline (pipeline.ts:75-82) calls applyCommands.

Verified: the fields, .strict(), and refusal of duplicates and invalid entries without repair are all at proposals.ts:64-95. The free-text `note` field exists, but an envelope is still the right design.
Verified. Line 56 says 'world coordinates'. POLYGON also has optional pitchDeg and downslope. There is no pixel, asset or page field.

There are 13 kinds, as stated. But 'none of them is … a terrace' is wrong as written: LEVEL_SURFACE is documented as 'A level exterior surface (a landing, a terrace)' (proposals.ts:44-45). It is a surface-level kind, not a terrace assembly, but terrace evidence does map to it. The rest holds: there is no guard/railing kind, no garage-door kind, no window-vs-door split, and no balcony kind.
Verified at proposals.ts:16. 'Neither describes it accurately' is the reader's judgement, not code fact.

The order (authority.ts:19), the mapping (:26-40) and HARD_EVIDENCE_STATUSES (evidence.ts:30) are correct. But the conclusion that a render fact 'never counts as hard evidence' needs a qualifier. In resolveQuantity, a lower candidate within max(tol(kept), tol(c)) counts as corroboration (authority.ts:88, :97-101), and PERSPECTIVE's tolerance is 0.25 m. So a PERSPECTIVE value within 0.25 m of a TECHNICAL_GEOMETRY value lifts that value to SOURCE_CORROBORATED, which is hard evidence. The emitters pass corroboratedBy.length > 0 through (emit.ts:321, :517, :608-609). The render value itself stays VISUAL_INFERRED, but it can promote another value to hard.

missed.statement: A render can promote a technical value to hard evidence. The pipeline emitters pass corroboratedBy.length > 0 straight into evidenceStatusOf.

An ACCEPTED family whose emitter fails is turned into decision UNKNOWN and emitUnknown is called without the realFeature gate (≥2 spatial proposals and ≥2 frames or technical). So the abstention rule in fuse.ts does not bound UNKNOWN emission on this path.

missed.statement: Renders are already processed today, but only on a publisher role claim and only as elevations. analyze.ts sends both ELEVATION and PERSPECTIVE_RENDER assets to the deterministic ELEVATION_EXTRACTORS. Only SITE_PLAN and DETAIL hit NOT_ATTEMPTED, and CHROME/UNKNOWN are skipped. A photo, interior render or mis-captioned image claimed as PERSPECTIVE_RENDER is therefore read as an elevation, with no pixel check. This is the concrete failure the 005R router would address, and the V0 baseline is the role claim itself.

The canonical model already has assembly kinds for most 005R exterior classes. AssemblyKindSchema = ROOF, DORMER, BALCONY, TERRACE, LOGGIA, CANOPY, PERGOLA, CARPORT, ENTRANCE, EXTERIOR_STAIR, FACADE, GARAGE, UNKNOWN. The hypothesis pipeline has families PERGOLA, CANOPY, CARPORT and EXTERIOR_STEPS. The gap is the view/router taxonomy and the feature-graph families, not the assembly vocabulary.

The capability registry makes cover status the deciding evidence for the roofed/open classes. CANOPY requires COVER_SURFACE and excludes NO_COVER_OBSERVED. CARPORT requires COVER_SURFACE plus VERTICAL_MEMBER and excludes NO_COVER_OBSERVED. PERGOLA requires repeated VERTICAL_MEMBER, HORIZONTAL_MEMBER and an observed NO_COVER_OBSERVED, and excludes COVER_SURFACE (PERGOLA_HAS_ROOF refused). Several of these requirements carry a cross-view flag and minimum frame counts. A 005R COVER_SURFACE vs NO_COVER_OBSERVED observation is therefore exactly the input these recognitions need. Registry TERRACE still says SUPPORTED, ANALYZER_V2, knownGaps [].

The independence counter is inflated on the railing path today. When a plan balustrade sighting is added to an existing solved feature, sourceCoverage.independentAssets is incremented by +1 with no assetId dedup (005P X21). At creation, by contrast, it is the count of distinct assetId. Because L2 is granted at independentAssets ≥ 2, a RAILING can be promoted without two independent assets. 005R cross-view counting of railings must not reuse this counter.

The remote vision path is off by default, but a server can turn it on with an environment variable. apps/analyzer-api reads ANALYZER_VISION=live and wires a VisionReasoner into the executor. The Anthropic provider injects publisher roles and published facts into the prompt. The Android/local analyzer has no vision provider by design. 005R's 'no publisher pixels to a remote model' rule therefore needs a check that ANALYZER_VISION stays deterministic, as well as the research isolation; it is not guaranteed by code on the server path.

The ELEVATION role already mixes two image classes that 005R wants to separate. A source package can label a photo-realistic orthographic render ELEVATION 'and be right', and the package does not record the difference. On the reference project all four elevations are photo-real renders. A TECHNICAL_ELEVATION vs EXTERIOR_RENDER router therefore has to split assets inside ELEVATION, not just re-label PERSPECTIVE_RENDER.

A local/offline VLM research harness already exists. research/analyzer-005m runs 2-8 B vision-language models (Qwen3-VL, SmolVLM2 and others) behind a local llama-server with --mmproj, with weights outside the repo. Balcony and railing geometry is hard-wired to an X-along / Z-depth facade. x0/x1 = extent.from/to and z0/z1 = mouthAt/backAt are used for every recess side, and railings use start/end {x: extent, z: mouthAt±0.05}. Returns, by contrast, switch axes for WEST/EAST. A balcony on a WEST or EAST recess would therefore be placed with swapped axes. The code is KNOWN; the effect has not been executed and is a HYPOTHESIS. Test: a synthetic side-recess upper storey with a fascia band on a LEFT/RIGHT elevation, checking the createBalcony footprint.

v2 elevation metric registration does not use the v1 isotropic scale. registerElevationV2 takes only the v1 extent and side and sets mpp = plan envelope span / silhouette width. For side views it chooses between the characteristic and walled depth by the ridge/terrain fit, refusing above 0.9 m. Any elevation-pixel JSON observation therefore depends on the plan envelope and ridgeY. ridgeY comes from levelsFrom on the section frame, or on all frames when no section exists.

The OWNER anchor `m3ea28300f9b3e` appears nowhere in the repository and has no pipeline output. - **Missing classes:** no shipping schema has a slot for the router classes (interior/exterior, photo, other). Seven of the 14 assembly classes have no model type: WINDOW, EXTERIOR_DOOR, GARAGE_DOOR, RAILING, COLUMN_POST, COVERED_TERRACE, and CANOPY_ENTRANCE as distinct from CANOPY. The research JSON therefore needs its own format that links to the existing types instead of reusing them.
- **Interior renders are read as façades:** in g2e, the 19 interior visualisations went through the façade extractors and produced roof-line, opening and loggia observations.
- **Two cases where I could locate the first bad operation:**

- **Four places where image values can be over-trusted:**
  - A render value within 0.25 m of a technical value can lift that value to hard evidence.
  - The pergola, canopy, carport and entrance assemblies are hard-coded to cross-view evidence, so a render-only one would be labelled geometric-inferred.

- Six git-tracked overlay SVGs each embed one publisher image as a `data:image` URI. They predate 005R and are not covered by the 005M isolation guard.
